phone-photos.name: Phone photography
phone-photos.blurb: Five steps from focus and exposure to a clear, well-composed photo.
phone-photos.title: Phone photography, simply
phone-photos.lead: Five steps from focus and exposure to a clear, well-composed photo.
phone-photos.result: Five steps from focus and exposure to a clear, well-composed photo.
phone-photos.note: Use ordinary photo mode and the main 1× camera.
phone-photos.s1t: Clean the lens and hold steady
phone-photos.s1b: Wipe fingerprints with a clean lens cloth. Hold the phone with both hands, brace your elbows and press gently. In low light, move somewhere brighter to reduce movement blur.
phone-photos.s2b: Tap the nearer eye for a portrait, or the important part of an object. Step back if the camera cannot focus close up. The box below marks focus; the nearby slider controls exposure.
phone-photos.s3b: Adjust brightness until the subject is visible and highlights retain detail. Lower it if white objects lose texture. For a dark face, increase exposure or change its position relative to the light.
phone-photos.s4b: Remove clutter or move the camera. Center a symmetrical subject, or place it near a third. Leave room in the direction a person looks. Use the grid as a guide rather than a rule.
phone-photos.s5b: Enlarge the photo to inspect the eyes or object edges. If only the subject is soft, refocus; if everything has directional blur, steady the phone or add light. Crop lightly, keep the original and export.
phone-photos.figAlt: Phone photographing roses and a cup by a window, with a rule-of-thirds grid.
phone-photos.figCap: The flowers sit on a third, not in the exact center. Light comes from the window.
phone-photos.diagram1: Put the focus box on the subject, then adjust the exposure slider.
phone-photos.diagram2: Dark, balanced and bright exposure diagrams. Preserve texture rather than simply making everything brighter.

window-light.name: Window-light portraits
window-light.blurb: One window is enough: choose soft light, position the subject, focus, expose and adjust the shadows.
window-light.title: Window-light portraits, simply
window-light.lead: One window is enough: choose soft light, position the subject, focus, expose and adjust the shadows.
window-light.result: One window is enough: choose soft light, position the subject, focus, expose and adjust the shadows.
window-light.note: Bring a phone or camera and a willing subject.
window-light.s1b: Use a window without direct sunlight on the face, or diffuse the sun with a sheer curtain. Switch off nearby ceiling lights to reduce mixed light colors.
window-light.s2t: Turn the face toward the window
window-light.s2b: Start about a metre from the window with the face around 45 degrees to the incoming light and the camera in front. The near cheek becomes brighter; adjust distance and angle to soften the shadows.
window-light.s3t: Focus on the eyes, expose for the face
window-light.s3b: Focus on the nearer eye. Adjust brightness until the forehead and cheek retain texture. Do not darken the face merely to preserve the view outside.
window-light.s4b: Turning toward the window gives more even light; turning sideways gives stronger contrast. If the far side is too dark, turn back slightly or use white card to reflect light. 45 degrees is a starting point.
window-light.s5b: Relax the shoulders and ask for a slow head turn. Choose a natural expression, enlarge the image to check eye focus and highlight detail, then crop distractions.
window-light.figAlt: A stuffed rabbit on a table beside a bright window, with soft side light.
window-light.figCap: Side window light: one bright side, one soft shadow. No extra lamps.
window-light.diagram1: Top view: window at upper left, subject in the middle, camera in front; white card on the right can fill shadows.
window-light.diagram2: From front light to side light, shadows increase. These direction diagrams simplify the effect; window size and distance also matter.

crop-compose.name: Image cropping
crop-compose.blurb: Choose a ratio, frame the subject, inspect the edges and export.
crop-compose.title: Image cropping, simply
crop-compose.lead: Choose a ratio, frame the subject, inspect the edges and export.
crop-compose.result: Choose a ratio, frame the subject, inspect the edges and export.
crop-compose.note: Keep the original. Cropping removes pixels and cannot recover missing detail.
crop-compose.s1b: Open Crop images on cv.cm and select or paste a photo. Processing stays in your browser without uploading the image.
crop-compose.s2b: Use 1:1 for a square, 4:5 for a portrait image or 16:9 for a banner. Ratio determines shape, not pixel dimensions. Check the destination preview before publishing.
crop-compose.s3b: Keep the important content inside the frame. Leave room in the direction a person looks, or center a symmetrical composition. Remove irrelevant background when the image feels crowded.
crop-compose.s4b: Inspect for distracting fragments. Leave space around headwear and feet in full-length portraits; avoid cutting exactly through wrists or knees when possible.
crop-compose.s5b: Reopen the export and check dimensions, sharpness and format. For a 1080 × 1350 image, keep at least that many source pixels in the selected area when possible. Otherwise crop less or choose a larger original.
crop-compose.figAlt: A bouquet of roses with a 4:5 crop rectangle over the strongest blooms.
crop-compose.figCap: The white frame is a 4:5 crop. Extra table at the edges can go.
crop-compose.diagram1: The same subject in square, portrait and wide frames; each ratio preserves a different area.
crop-compose.diagram2: The dark outline marks the retained area. The output ratio can differ from the original.

badminton-warmup.name: Badminton warmup
badminton-warmup.blurb: Ten minutes before you step on court.
badminton-warmup.title: 10-minute badminton warmup
badminton-warmup.lead: A warmup is the part video can actually help. It does not teach you to play. You still need a court, a partner, and usually a coach.
badminton-warmup.result: A warmup you can repeat before any game, plus a bag checklist.
badminton-warmup.note: This is a court aid, not a promise you will play badminton. Online video cannot deliver footwork or timing.
badminton-warmup.s1b: Light jog, skip, or side steps around the court. Raise heart rate before you stretch.
badminton-warmup.s2t: Open the joints you will load
badminton-warmup.s2b: Circles: ankles, hips, shoulders, wrists. Ten each way. Then walking lunges and side lunges — badminton is a lunge sport.
badminton-warmup.s3b: Twenty clears and twenty net shots on each side, slow then a little faster. No shuttle needed.
badminton-warmup.s4b: Do not open with smash contests. Short, controlled hits until the shoulder feels warm.
badminton-warmup.s5b: Gum-rubber court shoes, a spare grip, water, and shuttles. Cotton socks. Skip street shoes on a gym floor.
badminton-warmup.practice: Do this warmup before your next booked court. Share the checklist with a partner via Cloud clipboard if you want.
badminton-warmup.figAlt: Top-down diagram of a badminton doubles court.
badminton-warmup.figCap: Doubles court from above: net in the middle, short service line, rear doubles service line.

badminton-rules.name: Badminton scoring
badminton-rules.blurb: 21 points, win by two, how to serve.
badminton-rules.title: Badminton scoring and service rules
badminton-rules.lead: You can keep score after 15 minutes. That is not the same as playing. Use this so the first club night is less confusing.
badminton-rules.result: You can run rally-point scoring and a legal underhand serve.
badminton-rules.note: Reading rules does not make you a player. Footwork, timing, and shot selection need a court and a coach.
badminton-rules.s1t: Rally point to 21, win by two
badminton-rules.s1b: Every rally is a point, whoever served. First to 21 wins the game if they lead by two. At 29–29, the next point wins (30).
badminton-rules.s2b: Match is best of three. Change ends at the end of each game, and in the third game when a side reaches 11.
badminton-rules.s3b: Hit below the lowest rib, racquet shaft pointing down, into the opposite service court. The shuttle must land in.
badminton-rules.s4b: Singles: long and narrow. Doubles: short and wide. Even score, serve from the right; odd from the left.
badminton-rules.s5b: Serve above the waist, hitting the net on the serve without going over, or touching the net with the body or racquet during a rally.
badminton-rules.practice: Watch one match and call the score out loud. Then serve ten legal shuttles on a court.
badminton-rules.figAlt: Top-down diagram of a badminton doubles court.
badminton-rules.figCap: Service courts sit in front of the rear doubles line and outside the singles sideline.

pool-safety.name: Pool safety
pool-safety.blurb: First visit checklist. Not a swim class.
pool-safety.title: Pool safety for beginners
pool-safety.lead: Do not learn to swim from a webpage. Drowning is fast and quiet. This card is what to do before you get in, and why you still need a coach in the water.
pool-safety.result: A first-visit checklist and a clear line: this page will not teach strokes.
pool-safety.note: This is not a swimming course. Video cannot teach you to swim, and it cannot take drowning liability. Book a certified instructor.
pool-safety.s1b: Swim where a lifeguard is on duty. A friend on a phone is not a lifeguard. If there is no guard, do not get in.
pool-safety.s2t: Read the depth marks before you jump
pool-safety.s2b: If you cannot swim, stay in the shallow end and do not jump. Depth changes faster than it looks.
pool-safety.s3b: For young children, an adult stays in arm's reach. Floaties and rings are toys. They are not a substitute for a watcher.
pool-safety.s4b: Goggles, a cap if the pool asks for one, a towel, and water. Skip a heavy meal right before, and skip alcohol.
pool-safety.s5b: A certified instructor in the water is the way to learn strokes. This page stops at safety. That is the honest product.
pool-safety.practice: Pick a lifeguarded pool. Write the checklist on Cloud clipboard. Do not get in until a guard is on the stand.
pool-safety.figAlt: Three pool-safety reminders: never alone, lifeguard, floats are not supervision.
pool-safety.figCap: Three non-negotiables before any first visit.
pool-safety.icon3: A float is not a babysitter

healthy-boundaries.name: Healthy boundaries
healthy-boundaries.blurb: Slow trust, one no, no self-prove.
healthy-boundaries.title: Healthy boundaries in 15 minutes
healthy-boundaries.lead: You do not need a 100-tip office-war book. Today: stop oversharing, watch character, refuse in two sentences, and do not attack yourself when someone is unkind.
healthy-boundaries.result: A one-page card: three things you will not share this week, one refusal line, one observation.
healthy-boundaries.note: This is a same-day practice card, not therapy and not a personality diagnosis. It will not teach you to fight coworkers. Free on cv.cm.
healthy-boundaries.s1t: Do not treat everyone as a friend on day one
healthy-boundaries.s1b: Warmth is not the same as access. Greet people; keep salary, family fights, and opinions of coworkers off the table until time and behavior earn them. You cannot unsay a secret.
healthy-boundaries.s2t: Watch how they treat people who lost status
healthy-boundaries.s2b: Character shows when A is out and B is in. Loyalty that follows power is data. Write one observation. Do not announce that you have seen it.
healthy-boundaries.s3b: Gossip, fake concern, and “you are overreacting” are hooks. A short, dull line — “I would not know” or “anyway” — and you leave. Revealing that you have seen through them is extra fuel.
healthy-boundaries.s4b: No essay, no apology pile. “I cannot do that.” Optional: one fact. People who only respect you when you shrink will test a longer explanation.
healthy-boundaries.s5t: Isolated or insulted: do not self-attack
healthy-boundaries.s5b: Group coldness is often about them, not a hidden flaw in you. Do not write a confession to win them back. Do not prove you are good. Spend the hour on your own work.
healthy-boundaries.practice: Open Cloud clipboard. Write three things you will not share this week, one refusal line you can actually say, and one observation with no names if you prefer. Keep the note; do not send it.
healthy-boundaries.figAlt: Three reminders: slow trust, do not take the bait, do not self-prove.
healthy-boundaries.figCap: Three moves you can practice today. None of them need a confrontation.

portrait.name: Portrait photography
portrait.blurb: A complete path from lens, light and posing to full-length, half-length and detail photos.
portrait.title: Portrait photography, simply
portrait.lead: A complete path from lens, light and posing to full-length, half-length and detail photos.
portrait.result: A complete path from lens, light and posing to full-length, half-length and detail photos.
portrait.note: Use a phone or camera. Agree on clothing, framing and photo use beforehand; fashion examples here feature adults.
portrait.figCap: Still-life stand-ins for light, clothes, and a cafe table.
portrait.f2: Phone and a short portrait lens. Brand does not matter today.
portrait.f3: Chair at 45° to the window. Near side bright, far side soft shadow.
portrait.f6: Lolita is architecture: bonnet, bows, parasol. Shoot the dress as well as the face.
portrait.f7: JK-style sailor collar as adult street fashion on a hanger — not a hunt for students.
portrait.f8: Hanfu needs space for the collar and sleeves. Side light shows the cloth.
portrait.f9: Cafe window: foreground table, glass, shade. Same person, third background.
portrait.s1b: Choose one outfit and a simple background. A full-length view, half-length view and clothing detail give the set context, personality and texture.
portrait.s2b: Start with the main phone camera and avoid getting very close to the face. On a camera, an equivalent 50–85mm lens is a useful start. Step back and reframe to reduce close-perspective exaggeration.
portrait.s3b: Use a window or open shade and avoid patchy leaf shadows. Turn slightly toward the light for a bright near cheek and soft far-side shadows. White card can brighten the dark side.
portrait.s4b: Focus on the nearer eye and preserve texture in facial highlights. For gentle movement, 1/250 second is a possible camera starting point; raise shutter speed or add light if it blurs. With a phone, seek good light too.
portrait.s5b: Turn the body slightly, relax the shoulders and bring the face gently toward the camera. Hands can lightly hold fabric or a prop. Give one clear direction at a time, such as looking outside or turning slowly.
portrait.s6b: Keep the camera level and leave room for shoes and headwear. Show a dress silhouette or give hanfu sleeves space. Adjust head angle or light if a hat shadows the eyes.
portrait.s7b: Arrange face, collar and hands clearly. With adult sailor-collar fashion or other outfits, try front and slightly turned views. Keep hair and hands from crowding the collar, and background lines away from the head.
portrait.s8b: Choose a cuff, bow, weave or accessory. Side light reveals texture. Focus on the detail and avoid glare that erases the pattern; step back if the phone cannot focus close enough.
portrait.s9b: Check focus first, then expression, light and background. Keep one image of each framing. Reshoot on location if an essential photo is soft.
portrait.s10b: Remove distractions and keep natural frame edges. Match brightness and color across the set without forcing every image into one ratio. Keep originals, export the finished photos and share as agreed.
portrait.diagram1: Full length shows the silhouette, half length emphasizes the person, and a detail shows texture.
portrait.diagram2: A background line through the head distracts. Move the camera so the line clears the face and head.
portrait.diagram3: Top view: window at upper left, subject in the middle, camera in front; white card on the right can fill shadows.

algorithms.name: Algorithm basics
algorithms.blurb: Three complete examples explain maps, binary search and recursion: when to use them, how they work and what they return.
algorithms.title: Algorithm basics, simply
algorithms.lead: Three complete examples explain maps, binary search and recursion: when to use them, how they work and what they return.
algorithms.result: Three complete examples explain maps, binary search and recursion: when to use them, how they work and what they return.
algorithms.note: Read JavaScript variables, arrays, loops and functions. Run examples in your browser developer-tools Console or local Node.js.
algorithms.figCap: Trace the snippets. Do not memorize them.
algorithms.s1b: An algorithm turns input into output through finite steps. For example, take a sorted array and a target number; return a matching index, or -1 if absent.
algorithms.s2b: O(1) costs stay roughly constant; O(n) scans the input; O(log n) repeatedly halves it; O(n²) often compares every pair. Also count extra memory.
algorithms.s3b: A Map stores keys and values. In twoSum, each key is a number already seen and its value is the index. For current value 7 and target 9, look for key 2 to find the partner.
algorithms.s4b: For [2,7,11,15] and target 9: 2 finds no 7, so store 2→0. Then 7 finds 2→0 and returns [0,1]. Looking up first prevents the current index from matching itself.
algorithms.s5b: The data must already be sorted consistently with the comparisons. To find 8 in [1,3,4,8,12], compare middle value 4, keep the right side [8,12], then find 8 at original index 3.
algorithms.s6b: A function calls itself on a smaller input and has a stopping condition. Countdown appends n, then handles n−1. At zero it returns the collected result. Without a reachable stopping condition, calls continue.
algorithms.s7b: Return two distinct indices, or null. twoSum([3,3],6) returns [0,1]; twoSum([3],6) returns null. Assuming average constant-time Map lookup, time is O(n) and extra space is O(n).
algorithms.s8b: lo and hi include both ends, so use lo <= hi. Skip mid after comparing so the interval shrinks. Return an index or -1. Time O(log n), extra space O(1). With duplicates, it returns a matching position, not necessarily the first.
algorithms.s9b: For one lookup in unsorted data, scan. For repeated key lookups, use a Map. For sorted, indexable data, consider binary search. For naturally nested problems, consider recursion. Input conditions come before speed.
algorithms.s10b: The input is a nonnegative integer. countdown(3) returns [3,2,1]; countdown(0) returns []. Time, output space and call-stack space are O(n). For large inputs, use a loop to avoid exhausting the stack.
algorithms.diagram1: Target 9: record 2 at index 0; on reaching 7, find 2 and return indices [0,1].
algorithms.diagram2: Find 8: compare 4, then keep the right half. Pale empty cells represent discarded positions.
algorithms.diagram3: Each call decreases n by 1. Stop at zero and return the collected [3,2,1].

read-character.name: Read people
read-character.blurb: Watch the weak, the absent, and first-choice.
read-character.title: How to read people in 15 minutes
read-character.lead: You do not need a 100-tip book of villains. Today: watch how they treat people with less power, how they talk about the absent, and treat being chosen first as data — not a compliment.
read-character.result: Three dated notes: one on the weaker, one on the absent, one on first-choice. No verdict.
read-character.note: This is a same-day observation card, not a personality test and not a diagnosis. It will not teach you to label coworkers. Free on cv.cm.
read-character.s1t: Watch how they treat people with less power
read-character.s1b: Juniors, waiters, the colleague who just lost a project. Contempt, teasing, or a sudden freeze is data. Charm aimed only upward is also data. Write what happened, not a type.
read-character.s2t: Watch how they talk about people who left the room
read-character.s2b: Praise in the face and a cut when the door closes is a two-sided act. You do not need to join the cut, and you do not need to announce that you noticed.
read-character.s3t: If they chose you first, pause
read-character.s3b: Groups often pick the easiest person first — warm, available, low threat. Being chosen can be entry, not loyalty. Hold back the extra secrets and extra favors until time matches the warmth.
read-character.s4t: Feeling understood is not proof of character
read-character.s4b: A skilled talker can make every sentence feel exactly right. That can be care. It can also be mirroring. Wait for a day when they have nothing to gain from you.
read-character.s5t: Three notes. No label. No scene.
read-character.s5b: One line each: weaker, absent, first-choice. Skip names if you want. Do not confront, diagnose, or post the list. Observation is the practice; a verdict is extra.
read-character.practice: Open Cloud clipboard. Date three lines. Keep the note; do not send it. If you already did the boundaries card, this is the watch; that one is the no.
read-character.figAlt: Three observation reminders: the weaker, the absent, no verdict.
read-character.figCap: Three things to watch today. None of them need a confrontation.

clip.a1: Yes. Paste text and get a link, with no account. Notes are only reachable by URL and are deleted after 10 views or 24 hours.
clip.q2: Do I need to sign up?
clip.a2: No. Create a note, copy the link, and send it. There is no login and no public listing.
clip.a3: After 10 views or 24 hours, whichever comes first. The last view tells you the note is gone.
clip.q4: Can I share images and files?
clip.a4: Yes. Text stays in D1 (up to 64 KB). Images, video, and other files go to S3, up to 32 MB each.
clip.a5: There is no directory. Only people with the link can open a note, and it still expires.

watermark.q1: Does adding a watermark upload my photos?
watermark.a1: No. The browser canvas stamps the mark. Closing the tab discards the files. Export also strips EXIF.
watermark.q2: Can I watermark many photos at once?
watermark.a2: Yes. Add a batch, then download one file or a ZIP of PNG or JPEG.
watermark.q3: Can I use text and a logo?
watermark.a3: Both. Pin to a corner, center it, or tile the mark across the photo.
watermark.a4: No. This tool only adds a mark. It will not erase watermarks from photos.
watermark.a5: PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF in. Export PNG, JPEG, or WebP.

collage.q1: Is this a photo collage maker?
collage.a1: Yes. Combine photos into one picture in the browser. Nothing is uploaded.
collage.a2: Square, 4:5 portrait, 9:16 story, and 16:9 landscape are built in.
collage.q3: How many photos can I combine?
collage.a3: Layouts cover two to nine cells, including 2×2, 3×3, and split frames.
collage.a4: PNG, JPEG, or WebP, with quality control for the lossy formats.
collage.q5: Do my photos leave this device?
collage.a5: No. Processing stays in this tab. Closing the page discards them.

convert.q1: Can I convert HEIC to JPG?
convert.a1: Yes in browsers that can decode HEIC (Safari, and Chromium with support). Then download a JPG.
convert.q2: Can I convert WebP to PNG or JPG to PNG?
convert.a2: Yes. Shortcuts cover HEIC → JPG, WebP → PNG, PNG ↔ JPG, SVG → PNG, and ICO.
convert.q3: Are images uploaded to a server?
convert.a3: No. Conversion uses the canvas in this tab.
convert.q4: Can I convert several images at once?
convert.a4: Yes. Download one file or a ZIP of the whole batch.
convert.a5: Yes. Keep the original size or cap the longest side at 2048, 1920, 1280, or 800 pixels.

image-pdf.q1: Can I convert JPG to PDF or PNG to PDF?
image-pdf.a1: Yes. Drop JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, or HEIC photos and download one PDF.
image-pdf.q2: Can several photos become one PDF?
image-pdf.a2: Yes. Reorder the pages, then download a single file.
image-pdf.a3: A4, US Letter, or a page that matches the photo’s aspect ratio.
image-pdf.a4: No. Each image is fitted onto its page without cropping.
image-pdf.a5: No. The PDF is built in this tab.

audio.q1: Can I convert MP3 to WAV?
audio.a1: Yes. M4A, OGG, AAC, FLAC, and WebM also decode to WAV in the browser.
audio.a2: No. Web Audio decodes the file in this tab.
audio.q3: Can I choose the sample rate?
audio.a3: Keep the original rate, or export 44.1 kHz or 48 kHz.
audio.a4: Yes. Download one WAV or a ZIP of the batch.
audio.a5: Not yet. This tool writes WAV so the output stays uncompressed and on-device.

data.a1: Yes. Pretty-print or minify JSON in this tab. Conversion runs as you type.
data.q2: Can I convert CSV to JSON?
data.a2: Both directions: CSV → JSON and JSON → CSV.
data.q3: Does it encode Base64 and URLs?
data.a3: Yes. Encode or decode Base64 and URL components, including Unicode text.
data.q4: Can I turn Markdown into HTML?
data.a4: Yes, and HTML back into Markdown. Copy or download the result.
data.a5: No. You can also open a local file; it never leaves this tab.

qr.q1: Is this a QR code generator?
qr.a1: Yes. Type a URL or any text and download a PNG. Encoding runs in this tab.
qr.a2: No. The code is drawn on a canvas in your browser.
qr.a3: Higher levels (Q, H) survive more damage or logos on the code, but need a larger QR.
qr.a4: Yes. Pick foreground and background colors before downloading.
qr.a5: Short URLs fit a small code. A few hundred characters still work; very long notes will be rejected.

password.a1: Yes. It builds a random password with Web Crypto in this tab.
password.a2: No. Generating and copying stay on your device. Closing the tab discards them.
password.a3: Entropy is length × log2(charset). 16 mixed characters is typically 80+ bits.
password.a4: Yes. Toggle lowercase, uppercase, digits, and symbols. You can also skip look-alike characters.
password.a5: No. It uses crypto.getRandomValues with unbiased sampling.

word-count.a1: Yes. It counts words, characters, sentences, paragraphs, lines, and a 200 wpm reading time.
word-count.q2: How are Chinese or Japanese words counted?
word-count.a2: Each CJK character counts as one word. Latin text still splits on spaces.
word-count.a3: No. Counting is local. You can also open a text file from your device.
word-count.a4: Characters includes spaces. There is a separate count without whitespace.
word-count.a5: About 200 words per minute, rounded up to a whole minute.

resize.a1: Yes. Set exact width and height, or cap the longest side at 1920, 1280, or 800 pixels.
resize.a2: Yes. Export JPG or WebP and drag the quality slider. The estimated file size updates as you edit.
resize.a3: No. Decoding and encoding use the canvas in this tab.
resize.q4: Does it keep the aspect ratio?
resize.a4: On by default. Uncheck it to stretch to any width and height.
resize.a5: JPG, WebP, or PNG. HEIC and AVIF can be opened when the browser can decode them.

crop.a1: Yes. Drop a photo, drag the frame, then download the cropped image.
crop.a2: 1:1, 4:5, 9:16 story, and 16:9, plus a free rectangle.
crop.a3: No. Cropping is local to this tab.
crop.q4: Can I paste from the clipboard?
crop.a4: Yes. Ctrl/⌘ V pastes an image, same as the other image tools.
crop.a5: JPG, PNG, or WebP of just the selected region.

color.a1: Yes. Pick a color and copy hex, RGB, or HSL. Everything stays in this tab.
color.a2: In Chromium browsers the EyeDropper API can sample any pixel on screen. Other browsers still have the native picker.
color.q3: Can I type a hex code?
color.a3: Yes. Hex, rgb(), and hsl() all parse. Invalid input is ignored.
color.a4: WCAG contrast against white and black. 4.5:1 is the usual body-text floor.
color.q5: Is the color sent to a server?
color.a5: No. There is no network call.

pdf-jpg.q1: Can I convert a PDF to JPG?
pdf-jpg.a1: Yes. Each page is drawn in this tab and saved as JPG, PNG, or WebP.
pdf-jpg.a2: Yes. One page downloads as an image. Several pages download as a ZIP.
pdf-jpg.a3: No. pdf.js renders it locally. Closing the tab discards it.
pdf-jpg.a4: It paints a larger bitmap, sharper but heavier. Use 1× for small files.
pdf-jpg.a5: Yes. Image-only pages export as pictures. Text-only pages are rasterized too.

merge-pdf.a1: Yes. Add two or more PDFs, reorder them, and download one file.
merge-pdf.a2: No. Merging uses pdf-lib in this tab.
merge-pdf.a3: Yes. Use the arrows in the file list before downloading.
merge-pdf.a4: Encrypted PDFs often cannot be merged here. Unlock them first.
merge-pdf.a5: Pages are copied. Bookmarks and forms may be dropped.

phone-photos.a1: No. Use any phone with focus and exposure controls; their locations vary.
phone-photos.q2: What if cleaning does not fix blur?
phone-photos.a2: Check whether the subject is out of focus or the whole image has movement blur, then adjust focus or stability.
phone-photos.q3: Are thirds always better than centering?
phone-photos.a3: No. Compare both with the same subject and judge background, space and purpose.
phone-photos.a4: Yes. Optical lens switching differs from digital cropping; inspect detail and dimensions afterward.
phone-photos.a5: Use the main 1× camera, find good light, tap the subject to focus and adjust exposure.

window-light.a1: No. Adjust face direction first; white card is an optional aid.
window-light.a2: The face direction relative to the window; keep the camera position as consistent as possible.
window-light.a3: To reduce mixed light colors and isolate the effect of the window.
window-light.a4: Yes. Choose one with facial depth so you can inspect eye sockets, nose and cheeks.
window-light.q5: How do I change facial shadows?
window-light.a5: Turn toward the window for more even light, or sideways for more contrast. White card can fill the dark side.

crop-compose.q1: How do ratio and pixels differ?
crop-compose.a1: 4:5 describes shape; 1080 × 1350 describes pixel dimensions. Different sizes can share one ratio.
crop-compose.a2: It can improve composition but removes pixels; enlarging cannot recover absent detail.
crop-compose.a3: Cropping runs in your browser without uploading the image.
crop-compose.a4: To verify that its actual framing, dimensions and format fit the intended use.
crop-compose.q5: Must eyes sit on the upper third?
crop-compose.a5: No. Gaze, background and purpose determine the composition.

badminton-warmup.q1: How long should a badminton warmup be?
badminton-warmup.a1: About ten minutes: easy bounce, joint circles and lunges, shadow swings, then easy rallies. Do not walk on and smash first.
badminton-warmup.q2: Will this teach me to play badminton?
badminton-warmup.a2: No. Video is a front end for warmup, rules, and gear. Playing needs a court, a partner, and usually a coach.
badminton-warmup.a3: If you want to actually play, yes, at least for a few sessions. This page will not replace that.
badminton-warmup.q4: What should I bring to the court?
badminton-warmup.a4: Court shoes with gum rubber, a spare grip, water, and shuttles. Not street shoes.
badminton-warmup.a5: You can. Shoulders and ankles often disagree later. Ten minutes is cheaper than a week off.

badminton-rules.a1: Rally point to 21. You must win by two. At 29–29, the next point wins. Best of three games.
badminton-rules.q2: How do you serve in badminton?
badminton-rules.a2: Underhand, below the waist, racquet shaft down, diagonally into the correct service court.
badminton-rules.a3: Every rally scores, even if you did not serve. That replaced the old side-out system.
badminton-rules.q4: What is the difference in doubles service?
badminton-rules.a4: Doubles uses the short, wide service court. Singles uses the long, narrow one. Even score from the right.
badminton-rules.q5: Does reading the rules make me a player?
badminton-rules.a5: No. This card is so the first club night is less confusing. Footwork is still on court.

pool-safety.a1: No. Do not learn to swim from a webpage. This is a first-visit safety checklist. Book a certified instructor for strokes.
pool-safety.q2: How do I stay safe at a pool?
pool-safety.a2: Lifeguarded water only, never alone, read depth marks, and keep young children in arm's reach.
pool-safety.q3: Can children use floaties instead of supervision?
pool-safety.a3: No. Rings and floaties are toys. They are not a substitute for an adult in touch distance.
pool-safety.q4: Should I learn to swim online?
pool-safety.a4: No. Delivery is the problem, and drowning liability is the reason. Online material can only cover safety and what to bring.
pool-safety.q5: What should I bring to the pool?
pool-safety.a5: Goggles, a cap if required, a towel, and water. Skip alcohol. Confirm a lifeguard is on the stand before you get in.

one-page-site.q1: Do I need to buy a domain?
one-page-site.a1: No. Start with the URL provided by your hosting service.
one-page-site.q2: Why is the public page unchanged?
one-page-site.a2: Saving updates the local file. Publish again to update the public version.
one-page-site.a3: It starts with a contact link. Payments require a separately configured provider link with verified product, amount and currency.
one-page-site.q4: Is GitHub Pages the same as Direct Upload?
one-page-site.a4: No. Follow its repository and publishing-source setup; the workflow differs from Cloudflare Direct Upload.
one-page-site.q5: How do I check public access?
one-page-site.a5: Use a private window and another phone to check that no sign-in is required and the button destination is correct.

healthy-boundaries.q1: How do I set healthy boundaries at work?
healthy-boundaries.a1: Slow the secrets, watch how people treat the out-of-favor, refuse in two sentences, and do not self-blame when a group goes cold. This 15-minute card is that practice.
healthy-boundaries.q2: Is this a psychology course or therapy?
healthy-boundaries.a2: No. It is a free same-day practice card. It is not diagnosis, not treatment, and not a substitute for a licensed clinician if you are in real distress.
healthy-boundaries.q3: Should I cut off difficult people?
healthy-boundaries.a3: Not as a first move, and not as a public scene. Distance and dull replies are usually enough. A dramatic break tells them you are now an enemy.
healthy-boundaries.a4: Short, boring replies that give gossip nothing to work with. You are not obliged to explain your feelings to someone collecting them.
healthy-boundaries.q5: Can I save the practice card privately?
healthy-boundaries.a5: Yes. Cloud clipboard on cv.cm can hold the note. It deletes after 10 views or 24 hours. Do not put other people’s names if you would not want that leaked.

portrait.a1: Yes. Start with the main camera and prioritize light, distance and focus.
portrait.a2: No. One adult, one outfit and one location are enough; the clothing styles are examples.
portrait.q3: Do I need a wide aperture?
portrait.a3: No. Keep the required eyes and clothing in focus before prioritizing background blur.
portrait.a4: Check distance and camera tilt. Close perspectives enlarge features nearer the lens.
portrait.q5: What belongs in a portrait set?
portrait.a5: Full length establishes the silhouette, half length emphasizes the person, and a detail shows material or accessories.

algorithms.a1: Read variables, arrays, loops and functions. Use paper to track execution.
algorithms.q2: Where do I run the examples?
algorithms.a2: Use your browser developer-tools Console or local Node.js. Text & data does not execute code.
algorithms.a3: To avoid matching an element with itself. Test [3] with target 6 to catch this error.
algorithms.q4: Can binary search use unsorted input?
algorithms.a4: Not this implementation. It relies on ascending order to discard half the interval.
algorithms.q5: Can recursion handle arbitrarily large inputs?
algorithms.a5: No. Call-stack depth is limited. Use small nonnegative integers here and prefer a loop for large inputs.

read-character.q1: How do I read people at work?
read-character.a1: Watch how they treat people with less power, how they talk about the absent, and treat being chosen first as data. Write three dated notes. Do not issue a verdict. This 15-minute card is that practice.
read-character.a2: No. It is a free observation card. It is not diagnosis, not NPD labeling, and not a substitute for a clinician if you are in real distress.
read-character.q3: Should I confront them when I notice something?
read-character.a3: No. Announcing that you have seen through them is extra fuel. Distance is enough. The boundaries card is the no; this card is the watch.
read-character.q4: What if I am always chosen first?
read-character.a4: Pause before you over-give. Groups often pick the easiest person first. Warmth can be an entry, not loyalty. Hold secrets until time matches the warmth.
read-character.q5: Can I save the notes privately?
read-character.a5: Yes. Cloud clipboard on cv.cm can hold them. It deletes after 10 views or 24 hours. Skip other people’s names if you would not want that leaked.

compress-pdf.q1: Can I compress a PDF here?
compress-pdf.a1: Yes. Each page is redrawn as JPEG and packed into a new PDF in this tab.
compress-pdf.a2: No. pdf.js renders locally. Closing the tab discards it.
compress-pdf.q3: Will the file always get smaller?
compress-pdf.a3: Usually for scans and photo PDFs. An already-tiny text PDF may not shrink much.
compress-pdf.a4: No. Pages become images, so text is no longer selectable.
compress-pdf.q5: What do quality and resolution do?
compress-pdf.a5: Quality is JPEG compression. 1× is smaller; 2× is sharper and heavier.

split-pdf.q1: Can I split a PDF into pages?
split-pdf.a1: Yes. Each page becomes its own PDF, packed in a ZIP when there are several.
split-pdf.q2: Can I keep only some pages?
split-pdf.a2: Yes. Use a range like 1-3,5 and download one PDF with those pages.
split-pdf.a3: No. pdf-lib runs in this tab.
split-pdf.a4: Often not. Unlock the file first.
split-pdf.a5: Pages are copied. Bookmarks and forms may be dropped.

names.a1: Yes. It makes random given+family names or usernames in this tab.
names.a2: No. They are random combinations for mockups, games, or handles — not legal identities.
names.a3: Yes. Switch to username for adjective+noun handles, sometimes with digits.
names.a4: No. Generation uses Web Crypto locally.
names.q5: Can I copy the whole list?
names.a5: Yes. Copy list puts every line on the clipboard.

timezone.q1: How do I convert a time zone?
timezone.a1: Pick the source zone, the destination zone, and a date-time. The result is the same instant shown on the other clock.
timezone.a2: Yes. Conversion uses IANA zones, so New York switches between EST and EDT automatically.
timezone.a3: No. Intl.DateTimeFormat runs in this tab. Closing it discards the conversion.
timezone.a4: It is the same instant as ISO-8601 in UTC, useful for APIs, logs, and calendars.
timezone.a5: Common cities first, then every IANA zone the browser knows, including UTC.

lorem.q1: What is a lorem ipsum generator?
lorem.a1: It fills a layout with classic Latin-like placeholder text so you can judge spacing before the real copy is ready.
lorem.q2: Can I choose paragraphs or words?
lorem.a2: Yes. Switch among paragraphs, sentences, and words, then drag the count slider.
lorem.a3: It follows the usual dummy-text word list. It is not a translation of a real passage.
lorem.a4: No. The text is built from a local word list in this tab.
lorem.a5: Yes. Copy puts the whole block on the clipboard so you can paste it into a mockup.

units.a1: Choose a category, a from-unit and a to-unit, then type a number. The result updates in this tab.
units.q2: Can I convert cm to inches?
units.a2: Yes. Length includes mm, cm, m, km, inches, feet, yards, and miles.
units.a3: Temperature converts among °C, °F, and kelvin, including the offset, not just a scale factor.
units.q4: Are these US or imperial gallons?
units.a4: Volume uses US customary cups, fluid ounces, and gallons. Length and mass use the international yard and pound.
units.a5: No. The arithmetic runs in this tab. Closing it discards the numbers.

barcode.q1: Can I generate a barcode here?
barcode.a1: Yes. Code 128, Code 39, and EAN-13 draw in this tab. Download a PNG when it looks right.
barcode.a2: Code 128 holds letters and digits for labels and shipping. EAN-13 is the 13-digit retail product barcode.
barcode.a3: No. Encoding and drawing stay in this tab. Closing it discards the image.
barcode.a4: Phone cameras and USB scanners read these formats when printed with enough size and contrast.
barcode.q5: When should I use a QR code instead?
barcode.a5: Use the QR tool for URLs and longer text. Barcodes are for short IDs and product numbers.

meme.q1: Can I make a meme here?
meme.a1: Yes. Drop a photo, type top and bottom captions, then download a PNG. Nothing is uploaded.
meme.a2: Classic meme style: Impact or a heavy sans, white fill and a black outline.
meme.a3: No. Drawing stays in this tab. Closing it discards the image.
meme.a4: Yes. Paste or drop PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, or HEIC when the browser can decode it.
meme.q5: How is this different from watermark?
meme.a5: Watermark is for a logo or copyright mark. This tool is for large top and bottom captions.

text-to-speech.q1: Can I convert text to speech here?
text-to-speech.a1: Yes. Paste text, pick a voice, and press Speak. The browser reads it with voices already on your device.
text-to-speech.a2: No. SpeechSynthesis runs in this tab. Closing it stops playback.
text-to-speech.a3: No. The browser voice engine does not give an audio file, so this tool only plays sound.
text-to-speech.q4: Why is the voice list empty?
text-to-speech.a4: Some browsers fill voices after a moment, or they have none installed. Chrome, Safari, and Edge usually work.
text-to-speech.q5: Does it support Chinese or other languages?
text-to-speech.a5: If your system has that language pack, it appears in the list. The page does not fetch cloud voices.
